newsitem.title: USA: New-homes sales drop in April after March boom.
newsitem.headline: New-homes sales drop in April after March boom.

text.p: Sales of new homes dropped at the sharpest rate in six months during April, the Commerce Department said on Friday, though the decline followed the strongest sales month in more than a decade during March.

Sales fell 7.7 percent last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 772,000 units. But it came after a steep revision to March sales to show a 2 percent increase to 836,000 -- the strongest sales pace since 857,000 a year in April of 1986.
Previously, the department said March sales had fallen 2.5 percent to 813,000 a year. But it sharply revised that estimate, pushing March sales up significantly.

April sales came in lower than estimated by Wall Street economists, who had forecast sales would slip only to a rate of 800,000 a year. April was the first month this year in which the sales pace dropped below 800,000, possibly indicating some sizzle going out of the booming housing market.
Sales were flat or lower in every region of the country last month.
The biggest drop occurred in the West, where sales slipped 16.5 percent to 197,000 a year. Sales were down 6 percent to 345,000 in the South and fell 2.9 percent to 134,000 in the Midwest.
Sales were unchanged in the Northeast at an annual rate of 96,000 during April.

The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said rates for a 30-year mortgage loan averaged 7.92 percent in April, barely up from 7.90 percent in March. That compared with a 7.93 percent mortgage rate available a year earlier in April 1996.
On Tuesday, the National Association of Realtors said sales of existing, or used, homes also decreased in April, falling 2.4 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.06 million.

While April new-home sales were down, builders and real estate agencies kept their inventories lean. There were 286,000 new homes on the market in April, down from 287,000 in March. It was the lowest number of homes for sale since July 1993, when there also were 286,000 available to buy.
April's seasonally adjusted annual sales rate of 772,000 was 4.2 percent higher than the rate a year ago, in April 1996, when sales were running at 741,000 a year.
The average home sales price in April rose to $183,200 from $171,700 in March while the median sales price went up to $151,600 from $145,000.
